scope: Reactivated search; mandatory five steering papers remain in the preserved R7 literature audit. New primary methods support narrow contrasts, not firstness.

entries.title: Modular Arithmetic: Language Models Solve Math Digit by Digit
entries.method: Fisher-score neuron selection on no-carry arithmetic; natural activation interchange across several MLP layers and seven thresholds; scores hybrid result digits. Supplementary carry-inducing donors test whether a digit patch also moves the next digit. Includes single- and multi-digit tokenizers.
entries.result: Digit-specific hybrid outputs are already causally tested. Carry effects are explicitly investigated and interpreted as largely separate. A simple digit-circuit, carry-locus or tokenizer-generalization finding would overlap.
entries.limit: Reading supports an overlap warning, not a claim that every possible arithmetic computation question has been solved. No candidate selected from this source yet.

entries.title: Specialized Attention Heads in Early Word Reconstruction
entries.method_from_abstract: Within-word attention/weighted-norm selection followed by targeted ablation and activation patching across languages, tokenizers and model families.
entries.limit: General detokenization-head discovery is already claimed. Exact methods and possible distinct contrasts require the paper body; abstract is insufficient for a novelty verdict.
Search results or their absence do not establish firstness. No qualified novel question is inferred from these searches.

entries.method: Generated imperfect-information betting games; diagnostic axes summarize action dependence on private information. Axis coverage selects games rather than directly manipulating identical payoff partitions.
entries.result: Model capability profiles differ even at similar aggregate strength.
entries.candidate_relevance: A uses a fixed-payoff equal-size partition intervention; strategy fusion itself is known. Exact distinct contribution UNVERIFIED.

entries.method: Extracts four-in-a-row search trees from reasoning traces; fits full-tree/myopic/discount backup models; deletes and restores trace paragraphs by depth.
entries.result: Myopic fits predict moves better and shallow paragraphs restore much of the choice effect.
entries.candidate_relevance: B must separate logical reward time from text order and correct path sums. A generic myopia finding overlaps. Internal discount identification is not claimed.

entries.method: Potential differences preserve optimal policies under the stated MDP conditions; undiscounted terminal potential is normalized.
entries.candidate_relevance: B sets both route endpoints to zero and checks all complete path sums exactly. This identity only constructs the control; it is not a new theorem.

entries.method: Compares sequential elicited distributions with passive/active Bayesian oracles; ProteinWorld supplies priors and class-conditional observation models.
entries.result: Non-reasoning updates diverge from oracle and reasoning improves posterior fidelity and discovery performance.
entries.candidate_relevance: C examines selective response to likelihood-preserving versus likelihood-changing collection on the same record. Exact overlap/firstness still UNVERIFIED.

entries.method: Number-game posterior prediction/evaluation/generation; strong/default/weak/explicit prompts and thinking conditions. Weak Prompt only states positive examples.
entries.result: Prompt sampling story changes fitted size-principle behavior; strong/weak wording manipulation is already tested.
entries.candidate_relevance: Standalone C2 novelty rejected. Explicit all-trial versus censored selection is not identical to this Weak Prompt, but a prompt distinction alone is insufficient contribution.

entries.method: Fifteen1D targets, stateless versus batch draws, temperature1/top-p1; Wasserstein/KL and goodness-of-fit tests.
entries.result: Protocol-dependent sampling failures are already measured.
entries.candidate_relevance: D only retains a selective low-order-normal/high-order-error pattern under rule and full-table descriptions. Eight-category recoding prevents a multivariate-firstness claim. Grammar distribution differs from free-generation evaluation.

entries.method: Generated graph tasks include maximum bipartite matching; varies graph size/sparsity, prompts and exemplars, plus spurious-correlation connectivity cases.
entries.result: Advanced prompting/ICL does not reliably fix harder matching; node-mention heuristics are explicitly discussed for connectivity.
entries.candidate_relevance: E tests degree-preserving feasible/infeasible pairs crossed with resource reuse, not generic matching failure. Exact new law remains unverified.

entries.method: Ambiguous/unambiguous demonstrations and contextualization/aggregation path patches.
entries.factual_correction: Table9 has n3 ambiguous0/1/2 and n10 ambiguous0/3/5/7, not only a single7/10 condition.
entries.candidate_relevance: Neutral-example dose alone is too close to the prior ICL pool for this selection.

entries.method: Function-vector superposition, Q/K/V decomposition and position changes; ambiguous:unambiguous ratio2:1 in the reviewed setup.
entries.result: Fully ambiguous Bayesian midpoint also appears in Appendix M.
entries.candidate_relevance: Does not prove exact fixed-information neutral-addition duplication, but strongly limits generic dilution/aggregation novelty.

entries.method: Minimal yes/no number-game generalization with repeated samples; explicit strong/weak sampling-story intervention not confirmed in these methods.
entries.factual_check: Table1 reported GPT BinL .65±.01 and MaxL .42±.02 match the actual table.
entries.limit: Numbers and absence of a manipulation do not establish new firstness.

entries.method: RL-trained builder writes an external filesystem before later queries, evaluated with a frozen answerer and hidden reward queries.
entries.candidate_relevance: External/native distinction alone does not establish a novel internal-state question; not selected.

entries.method: Fixed factual candidate pools; compares generative likelihood, chat-template rescoring and explicit P(True); entity masking and semantic/human label audits.
entries.result: Candidate availability, ranking and final selection dissociate; verification gains depend on entity information and correctness criterion.
entries.candidate_relevance: Limits a generic knowing-versus-choosing/verification claim. These methods do not establish exact duplication of R9-A fixed-payoff information-partition contrast. Not a novelty proof in either direction.

entries.method: Random SCM per synthetic episode; shared mechanism across prior records, an intervenable manipulator and a held-out reactor; parses explicit graph/equation hypotheses. Interventions replace intercept terms while retaining incoming contributions, rather than hard do(X=v).
entries.candidate_relevance: Predictive success versus recovered mechanism and interactive discovery are already studied. Small bit/table substitution alone has insufficient contribution; this does not preclude every new causal-inference contrast.

entries.method: Trains recurrent architectures with a separate symbol axis and symbol-equivariant operations; tests Sudoku, ARC and mazes, including cardinality extrapolation.
entries.candidate_relevance: Architecture-enforced equivariance is not an exact experiment on frozen Gemma token renamings. Generic symmetry concepts are known; a distinct predictive frozen-model question has not yet been specified.

entries.method: N-back tasks across15 models; calibration threshold and1000 held-out sequences; target-letter head patching, attention location on errors, linear probes, sharpening versus removing competing identity.
entries.candidate_relevance: A generic target-located-but-misread or distractor-content-erasure claim is adjacent prior work. Most misses locate the target, whereas lure false alarms commonly attend to the lure; do not generalize the miss result to all error types. Body is accessible to Codex though GPT reported access failure.

entries.method: Controlled sensor logs with exact posterior cross original, forwarded copies, pointers, matched padding and independent sensors; self-reported probabilities converted into independent-reading units. Paired items, corrected tests and explicit equivalence controls.
entries.result: Copies shift evidence and implied commitment despite provenance labels; effects depend on repeated values rather than record count alone.
entries.limit: Simple copy-versus-independent-source counting is closely covered. Does not rule out every unproposed provenance mechanism.

entries.method: Regresses expressed-belief change on initial belief; separate LLM judge reads reasoning. Forecasting, ChangeMyView and review tasks cross prompts and CoT/debate.
entries.result: Positive slopes in51/54 CoT setups; reported association with Brier error.
entries.limit: A generic martingale-update diagnostic is known. OLS zero slope is not sufficient to prove full Bayesian rationality; judge-extracted beliefs are not direct latent states. This does not establish exact duplication of every synthetic update design.

entries.method: Same paired judge items use restricted first-position verdict logits versus generated verdict parsing, with full-vocabulary compliance recorded. Multiple code labels/models and source-cluster bootstrap.
entries.result: Compliance varies by model/task/code; the reported readout distortion is strongest on noncompliant items.
entries.limit: Supports the need to distinguish first-token scoring from a generated verdict. Not direct evidence about why this Gemma run emitted To or what its final answer would be.

Claude cited these for its proposed alternatives, mostly from abstracts/excerpts. Codex did not verify their detailed methods/results; exact duplication is not established. Current No-Go is lack of a qualified distinct question, not a proof from unread papers.

post_result_scope: Body checks added after both independent reviews; method/result overlap is limited to the read sections and cannot certify global novelty exhaustion.
